message.content: {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001784","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches for abdominal aortic aneurysm with phenotype labels aligned (all report abdominal aortic aneurysm; one is prevalent AAA but still endpoint-faithful). Among them, PGS001784 provides the clearest PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports a covariates-regressed-out/PGS-only Nagelkerke R² of 0.014661 in European evaluation (n=350,767), which is directly comparable across models and is below the provided local heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.02), supporting metric plausibility. Competing candidates either lack PRS-only metrics (PGS003972/PGS003973/PGS003429) or provide weaker/less directly comparable evidence (PGS002054 reports partial-r=0.0144; PGS000753 reports OR=1.37 per SD, moderate). However, confidence is not high because PGS001784’s reported AUROC (0.868) is a full-model metric with substantial covariate adjustment (age/sex interactions, 20 PCs) and cannot be treated as PRS-only discrimination, and several other direct-match models come from disease-focused AAA GWAS/meta-analysis contexts but do not report comparable PRS-only metrics in the provided metadata, limiting a definitive best-choice."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002738","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All four candidates are direct/near-direct matches to the target alcohol dependence spectrum, but none reports a PRS-only AUROC/R2, limiting comparability and making the choice sub-optimal. PGS002738 is the best-supported pick because it is explicitly aligned to the target concept (trait_efo=alcohol dependence; phenotyping_reported=Alcohol use disorder) and provides the strongest visible discriminative evidence via an odds ratio for high-risk stratification (OR top 10% vs rest=1.96, 95% CI 1.54–2.51) in a European evaluation sample (n=7,900). By contrast, PGS000201/PGS000202 target ‘problematic alcohol use’ / alcohol dependence measurement with DSM-5 criteria count and only report small incremental ΔR² (0.01192 and 0.00456) and betas, and PGS002739 is evaluated only in African American/Afro-Caribbean samples (less directly comparable if deployment ancestry is unspecified) despite a supportive OR (1.76). Main limitation: heterogeneous endpoints across candidates (AUD diagnosis vs DSM-5 criteria count) and lack of PRS-only discrimination metrics/covariate transparency (covariates unknown for PGS002738/PGS002739) prevent a high-confidence direct-match recommendation."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001261","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 19 candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris (trait_efo=angina pectoris) with generally acceptable endpoint alignment (Angina / ICD10 I20 / PheCode 411.3 variants). Among models with explicit PRS-comparable metrics, the snpnet PLoS Genet scores (PGS001260/PGS001261/PGS001262) report PGS-only AUROC (~0.58) and PGS R² (~0.012–0.013) with basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array), making them more directly comparable than candidates that report only full-model C-index/AUROC or only an OR. Within that snpnet set, PGS001261 (time-to-event angina pectoris) has the strongest reported PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC 0.58233; PGS R² 0.01228) and the highest full-model AUROC (0.74852) among the closely related endpoints, so it is the best-supported pick from the visible evidence. Main limitation: these snpnet models come from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper (\"across 813 traits\"), which domain guidance flags as often less externally robust; additionally, several newer ICD10/PheCode-based candidates show higher full-model C-index or stronger ORs but lack PRS-only metrics, preventing a high-confidence, apples-to-apples comparison."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001267","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 9 candidates are direct matches to ankylosing spondylitis by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported. Among them, PGS001267 provides the clearest PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports both PGS-only AUROC (0.7265, with CI) and PGS-only R² (0.0988), plus incremental AUROC, with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs) and a large European validation sample (n=67,425). PGS001268 is a close competitor with slightly higher reported metrics but is explicitly time-to-event (phenotyping_reported: TTE ankylosing spondylitis), which is a mild endpoint mismatch for a generic disease-risk target and makes it less straightforward as the primary direct-match choice. Other candidates either lack PRS-only AUC/R² (PGS001876, PGS002089) or report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates in a small single-population evaluation (Taiwanese EAS models PGS003420–PGS003424), reducing comparability. Limitation: the chosen model comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper (snpnet across 813 traits) and is very sparse (10 variants), which the provided domain guidance flags as potentially less robust for external generalization; this prevents a high-confidence designation despite good PRS-only metrics."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS005252","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates for aortic stenosis are present (PGS005252, PGS005254, PGS005255, PGS005256). PGS005252 is best supported in the provided metadata because it is explicitly aligned to the target endpoint (trait_reported/trait_efo: aortic stenosis; phenotyping_reported: incident aortic stenosis cases) and it provides the richest visible performance evidence among the direct matches (reported C-index 0.87 plus HR=1.92) with large European evaluation (n=446,895). The main limitation is that the reported discrimination is a full-model metric with substantial clinical covariate adjustment (multiple cardiometabolic comorbidities and risk factors), and no PRS-only AUROC/R² or incremental metrics are shown; therefore the PRS-specific contribution cannot be cleanly compared across candidates, keeping confidence below high. Competing direct-match models (PGS005254/PGS005255/PGS005256) report HRs (1.64; 1.53; 1.53) with simpler covariates but lack comparable discrimination metrics, leaving some unresolved uncertainty about which score is strongest as a standalone PRS."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001135","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates for the target trait (arthritis) are present, including PGS001135 (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to “Arthritis (nos)” / EFO: arthritis). Among the visible arthritis-labeled options, PGS001135 provides PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.53928; PGS-only R2=0.00291) plus full-model AUROC=0.67424 with basic covariates (age, sex, array type, genotype PCs), making its performance evidence more interpretable than arthritis-labeled alternatives like PGS004477/PGS004547 that report only an OR without PRS-only metrics and have unknown covariates. However, the best available direct-match evidence remains limited: the PRS-only performance for PGS001135 is modest and the model comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as often underperforming disease-focused models; additionally, the target ‘arthritis’ is heterogeneous and other strong models in the list are for specific arthritis subtypes (e.g., RA, gout, psoriatic arthritis) rather than the generic endpoint. These factors prevent a high-confidence, high-quality direct-match recommendation."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002727","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Multiple direct-match asthma PRS candidates are present. PGS002727 is the best-supported direct-match in the provided set because it targets a closely aligned endpoint (phenotyping_reported: pediatric asthma; trait_efo: asthma) and provides comparatively strong, PRS-informative effect-size evidence (OR per SD 1.57, 95% CI 1.55–1.60) alongside a large validation sample size (n=391,820) and moderate full-model AUROC (0.66) with an R² reported (0.04). However, the choice remains sub-optimal because the endpoint is pediatric-specific (not generic asthma), covariates are listed as unknown (reducing comparability), and several other asthma models report PRS-only metrics (e.g., UKB snpnet models with PGS-only R² ~0.037 and PGS-only AUROC ~0.618) but are from a pan-trait framework context and/or have less directly interpretable standalone PRS evidence than the strong OR signal here. These trade-offs prevent a high-confidence, clearly dominant selection from the visible metadata alone."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002755","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct EFO matches to atopic eczema, but several have endpoint mismatches: PGS003459/PGS003486/PGS004903 are evaluated on paradoxical (biologic-treated psoriasis) eczema rather than general atopic eczema risk, and PGS001773 targets moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis in Canadian cohorts with a very high full-model AUROC (0.93) that is not PRS-only and is therefore not comparable/likely covariate-driven per the provided guidance. Among the remaining general-disease endpoints, PGS002755 and PGS004587 both use incident atopic dermatitis with large European validation (n=337,910) and report HR (high vs low PRS); PGS002755 uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large variant coverage (1,090,702), which is structurally favorable for a polygenic trait compared with the sparse 23-variant GWAS-hits approach in PGS004587. Limitation: neither model provides PRS-only AUROC/R², and the HRs are modest (PGS002755 HR 1.249; PGS004587 HR 1.153), so the evidence does not support a clearly high-quality choice despite preferring PGS002755 on method/coverage and endpoint alignment."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS005168","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Multiple direct-match atrial fibrillation PRS candidates are present. PGS005168 is best supported in this context because it is a disease-focused, large multi-cohort meta-analysis PRS-CS model explicitly targeting atrial fibrillation (phenotyping_reported: \"Atrial fibrillation\"), with strong reported discrimination in European validation (C-index 0.8718, 95% CI 0.8657–0.878) and a substantial per-SD effect size (HR 1.6663). Its covariates include basic demographics plus CHARGE-AF, which introduces some risk of covariate-driven inflation of the full-model metric; however, the endpoint alignment remains direct and the overall evidence package (study archetype, multi-cohort development, and strong effect size) is stronger than older UKB-only framework scores (e.g., snpnet/bigstatsr portability papers) and than candidates that are explicitly horizon-packaged (e.g., \"5-year risk\") or have weaker/less informative performance reporting. Confidence is moderated because many candidates report only full-model metrics (often with unknown or heterogeneous covariates), making cross-model performance comparability imperfect, and because the inclusion of CHARGE-AF means the reported C-index is not a PRS-only metric."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001263","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All four candidates are direct matches at the concept level (atrial flutter explicitly or via the combined AF/flutter endpoint). PGS001263 has the best phenotype alignment (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are both 'Atrial flutter') and it reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates=0.61716; PGS R2 no covariates=0.02517) with basic covariates; its PGS-only R2 is below the provided heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.0157) but not grossly inconsistent given scale differences, supporting basic sanity. However, confidence is limited because the strongest competing models (PGS001841, PGS002050) come from a portability framework paper and do not report PRS-only AUROC/R2 here (only partial-r), making performance comparison across candidates incomplete; additionally, PGS001263 itself is from a pan-trait UKB framework ('across 813 traits'), which domain guidance flags as a generalizability concern. Given the need for direct atrial-flutter specificity and the presence of explicit PRS-only metrics, PGS001263 is the best-supported direct-match choice, but overall evidence quality remains sub-optimal."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000327","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Both candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo, but PGS000327 has substantially better endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported is explicitly “Autism spectrum disorder” vs PGS002790’s “Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)”), making it the cleaner direct ASD PRS. PGS000327 also shows stronger visible performance evidence (full_model_r2=0.0245 and OR per SD=1.33 [1.30–1.36]) than PGS002790 (partial R²=0.00546; no effect sizes shown), with broadly similar EUR-only evaluation ancestry. Main limitation: neither model reports clearly PRS-only (no-covariate) AUC/R², so the comparison relies on endpoint alignment plus non-PRS-only metrics/effect size reporting, lowering confidence from high."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000452","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All listed candidates are direct matches to basal cell carcinoma by trait_reported/trait_efo, with generally comparable (mostly basic) covariate adjustment (age/sex/batch/PCs) in the Cancer PRSweb family. Among models with reported discrimination, PGS000452 has the strongest visible performance package in this context: full-model AUROC 0.632 (95% CI 0.616–0.647) plus the largest reported Nagelkerke pseudo-R² (0.0487) and a strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.663, 95% CI 1.57–1.761), outperforming close siblings (e.g., PGS000454 AUROC 0.632 but slightly lower OR 1.661; PGS000456 AUROC 0.63). Other candidates either show materially weaker AUROC (e.g., PGS000447/448 ~0.59) or lack comparable AUROC/R² reporting (e.g., PGS003416/PGS003417/PGS005207 report ORs only; PGS000730 has unknown covariates). Main limitation: none of the candidates report explicit PRS-only AUROC/R², so comparisons rely on full-model metrics and effect sizes that may be partly covariate-influenced; several near-tied Cancer PRSweb siblings make the top choice not unequivocal."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002032","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All three candidates are direct matches to the target EFO concept (bilirubin metabolism disease), but they differ in endpoint specificity and evidence quality. PGS001824 and PGS002032 both target the most specific aligned endpoint (“Disorders of bilirubin excretion”; trait_efo exactly bilirubin metabolism disease) and come from the same publication with identical reported partial correlation (partial-r=0.0716, EUR validation). Between these two near-clones, PGS002032 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with far higher variant coverage (19,768 vs 22), which is a supportive structural signal when other evidence is essentially tied. PGS000924 reports strong-looking discrimination metrics (including PGS-only AUROC/R2), but it is from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper and uses a broader composite/time-to-event phenotype (“Disorders of porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism (time-to-event)”), which the provided domain guidance flags as a common generalization-risk pattern; additionally its PGS-only R2 (0.218) exceeds the provided local h2_obs estimate (~0.089), raising a sanity-check concern about metric comparability/scale. Main limitation: neither PGS001824 nor PGS002032 provides AUROC or PRS-only R2, so the selection relies primarily on endpoint alignment plus method/variant-count heuristics rather than directly comparable discrimination metrics."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002786","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All three candidates are direct matches to the target disease spectrum (bipolar disorder / bipolar I / bipolar II) and are near-clones in study family (same publication, SDPR method, PGC training, EUR-only GWAS/EVAL, similar ~935k–949k variant counts, similar validation Ns ~2.2k–2.5k). However, endpoint fidelity is unclear/weak across the set because `phenotyping_reported` fields describe non-diagnostic cognitive/behavioral measures (e.g., pattern comparison; DSM5 depression; sluggish cognitive tempo) rather than bipolar disorder case-control status, and the only reported metric is a small partial R² (full_model_r2 ~0.0025–0.0031) with no PRS-only AUC/R². Given the target is broad ‘bipolar disorder’, PGS002786 is the closest concept match by `trait_reported`/`trait_efo` and has the largest variant count, but differences versus the subtype siblings are minor and the phenotype/metric limitations prevent a high-quality direct recommendation."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001033","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All three candidates are direct matches at the EFO level for the target concept (blood coagulation disease), but they differ in endpoint specificity and evidence completeness. PGS001033 maps directly to the target EFO (blood coagulation disease) and provides explicit discrimination metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.634 and full-model AUROC 0.656 with basic covariates), whereas PGS001826 and PGS002034 target a narrower congenital clotting-factor deficiency EFO and report only partial correlation (~0.056) without AUROC/R², making performance comparison less direct. However, PGS001033 is from a pan-trait sparse UK Biobank framework paper and is extremely sparse (1 variant) with a time-to-event phenotype, both of which are warning signals for robustness/generalizability; this prevents a high-quality designation despite being the best-supported direct-match option in the provided metadata."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS004153","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Multiple direct-match candidates for breast carcinoma are present. Among the visible candidates, PGS004153 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) is a direct breast cancer model (trait_efo=breast carcinoma; phenotyping_reported=Breast cancer) with empty covariates (covariates=0, reducing concern that performance is driven by clinical risk-factor packaging) and the strongest reported discrimination in the provided set (full_model AUROC 0.6625 with R² 0.0764 and OR per SD 1.83). Competing direct-match models include PGS004040/PGS004025 (LDpred2 variants) with very similar AUROC (~0.6598) and slightly lower R² (~0.0736–0.0739), and older disease-focused models such as PGS000007 (AUROC 0.78) but with explicit age/sex covariates and a phenotype label of personal history, making its AUROC less directly comparable as PRS-only evidence. Confidence is Moderate rather than High because many direct-match candidates exist with close performance (especially within the 2023 five-biobank evaluation family), and most reported AUROCs are full-model rather than explicitly PGS-only, limiting strict comparability across studies."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000316","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All listed candidates are direct matches to celiac disease via trait_efo, but several have endpoint restrictions or framework-study origins. PGS000316 has strong phenotype alignment (phenotyping_reported: Coeliac disease), is disease-focused (pilot clinical-care diagnosis aid study rather than a pan-trait/portability framework), and reports a high AUROC (0.879, European validation) with a very large validation sample size (n=379,767), providing comparatively robust performance evidence among the direct-match set. Key limitation: the reported AUROC is a full-model metric (no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2), and covariates are listed as Unknown, so the degree to which discrimination reflects the PRS alone versus covariate contribution cannot be verified from the provided metadata; this keeps confidence at Moderate and prevents treating higher full-model AUROC values (e.g., PGS000040 at 0.90) as definitively superior without PRS-only comparability."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003428","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo=cervical carcinoma; phenotyping_reported is cervical cancer/incident cervical cancer). However, most reported discrimination is full-model AUROC/C-index with covariates, and only one model (PGS001299) reports explicit PGS-only metrics—those are weak (PGS-only AUROC 0.552; PGS R2 0.00263) and it comes from a pan-trait UKB framework paper, which the provided domain guidance flags as often less reliable for external performance. Among the remaining disease-endpoint models, PGS003428 is preferred because it is from a cervical-phenotype GWAS meta-analysis context and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred) with very large variant coverage (2,894,555), which is a positive structural signal versus small GWAS-hit scores (PGS000073/PGS000784) and a weaker-performing lassosum model (PGS003389; AUROC 0.563). The main limitation is that PGS003428 still lacks PRS-only performance metrics (only a C-index 0.613 and HR 1.33 with age/smoking covariates), so the evidence does not cleanly establish it as a high-quality standalone PRS over the other direct-match options."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001174","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct/near-direct matches to cholelithiasis, but most lack PRS-comparable discrimination metrics (AUC/R²) and/or have endpoint broadening. PGS001174 is the only model here reporting explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC no-covariates=0.62342; PGS R² no-covariates=0.02808) plus incremental AUROC (0.04311) with basic covariates, and its PRS-only R² is plausibly below the provided EUR heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.0214; h2_liability=0.1372), supporting internal sanity. However, it is a pan-trait UKB framework score (\"across 813 traits\"), which domain guidance flags as a generalization risk, and its phenotype is time-to-event rather than a generic diagnosis endpoint. Competing models include disease-endpoint ICD10 K80 scores (PGS004476/PGS004546) and a multi-ancestry GWAS-derived EAS-evaluated score (PGS005150), but these provide only effect sizes (OR/β) without PRS-only AUC/R², making them hard to rank confidently against PGS001174 on comparable performance; additionally, PGS001861/PGS002072 broaden the endpoint to include cholecystitis. Net: a direct-match exists and PGS001174 is best-supported by available comparable metrics, but evidence limitations and framework/TTE concerns prevent a high-quality designation."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002237","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All listed candidates are direct matches to chronic kidney disease via trait_efo, but they vary in endpoint fidelity and how interpretable the reported performance is. PGS002237 is the most disease-focused, endpoint-specific CKD model in the set (CKD stage ≥3; phenotyping_reported: eGFR <45 ml/min/1.73m2) and comes from a CKD-focused publication (“Genome-wide polygenic score to predict chronic kidney disease across ancestries.”). It also reports a reasonably strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.32–1.65) and shows multi-ancestry evaluation, supporting robustness. The main limitation is that the only discrimination metric shown is a full-model AUROC (0.78) with a heavy clinical covariate set (including hypertension, diabetes, BMI, medication use, etc.), and no PRS-only AUROC/R² is provided, so the AUROC is not directly comparable as standalone PRS performance. Competing models either have weaker/less-aligned phenotypes (e.g., PGS000728 uses eGFR as phenotype; PGS000859 is tied to a diabetes subtype), are framework-style sparse UKB scores with weak PRS-only metrics (PGS001272), or are benchmarking-family CKD-or-dialysis scores with modest full-model AUROC (~0.59) and limited disease-focused context. Given missing PRS-only metrics across most candidates and covariate-driven performance concerns, the best pick is supported but not cleanly decisive."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001783","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Multiple direct-match COPD candidates are present (PGS001332/PGS001333/PGS001334/PGS001783/PGS001788/PGS004466/PGS004536; plus chronic airway obstruction mapped to COPD: PGS001850/PGS002062). Among these, PGS001783 is a direct COPD endpoint with a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto; 884,139 variants) and is developed from a large multi-biobank GWAS cohort list, which is structurally stronger than the sparse UKB pan-trait snpnet COPD scores (PGS001332/PGS001333/PGS001334) and the UKB portability scores (PGS001850/PGS002062). However, the evidence remains limited/partly non-comparable across candidates: several models report only full-model AUROC or partial-r, and the Commun Biol J44 models (PGS004466/PGS004536) provide only per-SD ORs with unknown covariates and no PRS-comparable AUC/R2, making it hard to cleanly rank them against PRS-CS models. Between the two PRS-CS-auto COPD models, PGS001783 has higher reported PRS-comparable R2 (0.038092 vs 0.0163 for PGS001788) and slightly higher AUROC (0.74 vs 0.715), but both are evaluated in EUR only and PGS001783 has a much smaller validation sample (n=7,128), so confidence is not high."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS004621","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates for cirrhosis are present (PGS000726, PGS000776, PGS004621), alongside alcohol-specific cirrhosis scores (PGS000704, PGS001777, PGS004913) that are less aligned to the generic target “cirrhosis of liver.” Among the direct matches, PGS004621 has the strongest overall evidence package in the provided metadata: it targets “Cirrhosis” with trait_efo exactly “cirrhosis of liver,” uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large variant coverage (1,089,806), and is evaluated in Europeans with a very large validation sample size (n=1,153,995). Competing direct-match models are much sparser (PGS000726: 12 variants; PGS000776: 9 variants) and/or have endpoint ambiguity (PGS000776 phenotyping_reported references an incident/time-to-event hospitalization endpoint in an at-risk NAFLD population despite being described as alcohol-related in method/trait fields). The main limitation is that none of the candidates report clearly PRS-only discrimination (PGS-only AUROC/R²); the available AUROC/C-index values are full-model style metrics, making cross-model performance comparison uncertain and preventing a high-confidence pick."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002042","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS001835, PGS002042), both aligned to the target with identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported = \"Corneal dystrophy\" and from the same UKB portability publication with similar training (UKB; n=391,124), validation size (n=19,321), ancestry distribution, and basic covariates (sex, age, birth date, deprivation index, 16 PCs). Neither reports PRS-comparable AUC/R2; the only visible performance signal is partial correlation, where PGS002042 is modestly higher (partial-r 0.0471 vs 0.0384). Given near-identical endpoint and study context, this small but consistent metric edge plus the more genome-wide shrinkage-style method/greater variant coverage (LDpred2; 59,944 variants vs penalized regression sparse 38 variants) supports selecting PGS002042. However, because both models come from a portability framework study and lack standard PRS-only AUC/R2 (limiting comparability and strength of evidence), the overall direct-match recommendation remains sub-optimal rather than high-confidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003725","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates for coronary artery disease are abundant and several are endpoint-faithful (e.g., PGS000013, PGS002244, PGS003446, PGS003725/3726/3727). Among these, PGS003725 is best supported by a combination of (i) direct phenotype alignment (phenotyping_reported: coronary artery disease), (ii) disease-focused multi-ancestry development/validation context (Nat Med 2023; multi-ancestry evaluation listed), (iii) modern genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with substantial variant coverage (1,296,172), and (iv) strong reported per-SD effect sizes (HR 1.75; OR 2.14). Main limitation: the context does not provide PRS-only discrimination metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R²) for PGS003725 (or most competitors), making cross-model performance comparability uncertain; additionally, closely related sibling models from the same publication family (PGS003726/PGS003727) appear very similar on visible fields, so the preference for PGS003725 is not definitive."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001331","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All three candidates are direct matches to Crohn disease (trait_efo=Crohn disease). PGS001331 and PGS001330 come from the same pan-trait UK Biobank sparse snpnet framework paper (a known weaker study archetype for external generalisation per provided domain knowledge), but they report explicit PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R²) with basic covariates only. Between these two siblings, PGS001331 has slightly better reported discrimination (PGS-only AUROC 0.579 vs 0.576; full-model AUROC 0.613 vs 0.603; incremental AUROC 0.027 vs 0.024) with similar endpoint alignment, so it is the better-supported pick within that family. PGS004254 reports a higher full-model AUROC (0.72) and an OR (2.18), but it lacks PRS-only AUROC/R² and therefore its full-model AUROC is not directly comparable as standalone PRS evidence; additionally, its publication context is not clearly a Crohn-focused PRS development study from the visible metadata. Overall, a direct-match exists, but the best-supported choice is limited by reliance on a pan-trait framework score and by non-comparable/missing PRS-only metrics for the newer alternative, so the direct-match recommendation is sub-optimal rather than high-confidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS005170","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match dementia models are present (e.g., PGS000929/PGS000946/PGS001827/PGS002035/PGS004281-004284/PGS004318/PGS005170).
